transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-08 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Jae Kim (Redwood SE), Luis Romero (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (CTO, Nimbus), Priya Nair (Platform Eng), Ethan Morales (SecOps)

Summary auto (auto-gen may be rough): demo of rate-slicing, org/project key patterns, and console walkthrough focused on multi-tenant controls and quota/burst handling.

[00:00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro from our side, I'm Sofia, I'm the AE working with Nimbus, with Jae and Luis from SE. Marcus, Priya, Ethan, can you do quick intros?
[00:00:12] Marcus: Yeah, Marcus Lee, CTO, leading infra and platform. we've been evaluating inference providers for personalization and checkout bots.
[00:00:20] Priya: Priya - platform engineering; we're mostly on GCP, some on-prem for PCI workloads.
[00:00:25] Ethan: Ethan, security ops, I'll be looking at compliance, SSO, KMS, audit logs.
[00:00:32] Sofia: Great. the agenda: quick qualification, then demo of the Console + API patterns for org and project keys, adaptive rate slicing and quota policies, and then next steps.
[00:00:45] Jae: I'll jump into the console and run a live sketch of how rate slicing would work for your team. heads up, i'll also show the Optimize recommendations for batching and quantization — the plan that reduces cost for high-throughput workloads.
[00:00:58] Marcus: Sounds good. just to be explicit — our main must-haves are 95th latency under 120ms for shorter prompts, ability to sustain spiky traffic (up to 800 QPS for personalization calls), and strict tenant isolation for checkout data.
[00:01:12] Priya: Also, we prefer Private deployment for checkout, potentially Dedicated for lower-sensitivity features.
[00:01:18] Sofia: Understood. for the demo I'll show a hybrid pattern — Private/Dedicated for payment-sensitive flows and Hosted for lower-sensitivity personalization.
[00:01:28] Luis: small note, when we say "org key" in the console we mean the top-level key for billing and tenancy and project keys for per-app segmentation. we sometimes see the phrase "project token" in other docs — it's the same idea.
[00:01:42] Ethan: quick question before demo — how does Redwood handle audit logs and KMS for Private? we need HSM/KMS integration and immutable audit trails.
[00:01:51] Jae: good question. for Private deployments we integrate with customer KMS (Cloud KMS or HSM via KMIP) and we capture detailed request/response metadata in audit logs — you can stream those logs to your SIEM. there's also an export for immutable storage.
[00:02:05] Priya: and SSO?
[00:02:06] Jae: SSO via SAML/OIDC on the control plane; RBAC is configurable per-org and per-project.
[00:02:12] Marcus: OK. let's see the console.
[00:02:15] [00:02:15] Jae: (screen) so here's the main Console. top-left is the org view, you can see org-level quotas and billing thresholds. i'm going to create a project key called "checkout-service" and then a project key called "personalization" — you can bind different quota and routing policies to each.
[00:02:34] [00:02:34] Jae: (typing) i'll set checkout-service with a concurrency cap and a hard p95 latency SLO; for personalization i'll enable adaptive rate slicing — that means the router will allocate slices of capacity dynamically based on observed QPS and priority lanes.
[00:02:49] Priya: are those slices sticky per-api-key, or do they float across keys?
[00:02:53] Jae: they are keyed to the project key, but we support sticky lanes for warmed KV cache for low entropy prompts; otherwise it's floating to maximize utilization. note: our "KV cache" shows as "KV cash" in some transcriptions, haha, but it's the cache.
[00:03:05] Marcus: what's the behavior during a spike when checkout and personalization spike together? we can't risk checkout calls getting throttled.
[00:03:12] Luis: the routing policy supports priority bands. you can mark checkout-service as high-priority and personalization as best-effort. under pressure we can fall back checkout to Dedicated or Private slice reserved capacity — the router will preempt lower priority slices.
[00:03:28] Ethan: will preemption drop requests or queue them? we need graceful degradation.
[00:03:32] Jae: there are options — soft-queue (short backoff), prioritized queueing, and immediate fallback to a smaller model variant. we typically recommend a 3-tier fallback: smaller model quantized variant, queue with 200ms jitter, then 429 if exhausted.
[00:03:47] Priya: Can we set per-org daily hard token quota and per-project concurrency?
[00:03:51] Jae: Yes. Console shows org-level caps, project-level caps, and per-key rate windows — tokens, requests/sec, concurrency windows. you can also configure leaky-bucket versus fixed-window behaviors.
[00:04:03] Marcus: about billing — if we reserve Dedicated slices for checkout, how do we avoid paying for idle capacity?
[00:04:09] Sofia: we recommend a hybrid: reserved baseline for critical flows and burst routing to hosted capacity for spikes. We can model cost in the pricing worksheet we'll send — it shows tradeoffs: reserved capacity reduces per-token cost but you pay for baseline; burst routing uses hosted and is metered.
[00:04:25] Marcus: good. can you show adaptive rate slicing in a simulated spike?
[00:04:28] [00:04:28] Jae: starting simulation — injecting a 10x spike on personalization while checkout stays steady. you can see slices for personalization grow until they hit org cap; checkout slice remains pinned. at 30s mark the router engages priority preemption and reduces personalization slice.
[00:04:47] [00:04:47] Priya: that graph latency spike around 00:04:35 looks like p99 to 450ms for personalization — acceptable. checkout p95 inverted remains under 90ms.
[00:04:58] Marcus: what's the monitoring story? We need token-level, route-level tracing and per-key cost split for billing.
[00:05:04] Luis: Console gives token-level cost breakdown, per-route dashboards, span traces integrated with your APM (we push trace ids). you can export raw usage to BigQuery for downstream billing.
[00:05:15] Ethan: security again — if we're on Private, who has access to logs? can Redwood read unencrypted payloads?
[00:05:20] Sofia: for Private deployments the control plane can be customer-managed. payloads can be encrypted end-to-end and keys live in your KMS. Redwood does not have access to plaintext unless explicitly given; that's part of the on-prem package.
[00:05:33] Ethan: good. need that in writing.
[00:05:36] Sofia: we'll attach the SOC2 pack and a Private deployment security brief.
[00:05:40] Marcus: one more question — how do you handle quota inheritance? eg org cap of N, and projects have percent allocations, what happens on underutilization?
[00:05:49] Jae: projects get reserved percentages; unused allocation can be pooled and borrowed by other projects if you enable shared-pool borrowing. you can set hard boundaries to prevent borrowing for compliance-sensitive projects.
[00:06:01] Priya: can you demo the API payload for switching keys and performing sticky routing?
[00:06:06] [00:06:06] Jae: sure. hitting the API — sample curl with header x-api-key: project_checkout_key. notice the route header x-rd-priority: high. the response returns x-rd-slice-id and x-rd-lane. you can also opt into sticky lanes with cache-key in the request.
[00:06:26] Marcus: any SDK differences? we use Go and Node on backend.
[00:06:30] Luis: we have official SDKs for Go, Node, Python. the SDKs handle retry backoff, batching and token accounting. we also publish a middleware for common frameworks.
[00:06:41] Priya: about Optimize — you mentioned model/quantization recommendations. can Optimize provide batch size and quant profile tuned for our prompt shapes?
[00:06:49] Jae: yes, Optimize runs a short profiler on a sample workload and suggests batching, kv-cache warmup strategies, and quantization profile that keeps latency within SLOs while lowering cost. we'll show an example report.
[00:06:59] [00:06:59] Jae: uploading a sample Optimize run — here's the recommendation: batch size 8 for personalization, enable prefix caching for user history, use int8 quant for the large model implies ~2.4x cost improvement with 5-10% latency variance.
[00:07:18] Marcus: can we test that with our sample dataset?
[00:07:20] Sofia: yes, pilot will include a sample run with your payloads.
[00:07:23] Priya: timeline — we want pilot next week if possible.
[00:07:27] Sofia: we can start pilot Tues 2027-06-10, run 2 weeks. i'll send invite after call.
[00:07:33] Ethan: for pilot will you provision a dedicated slice or hosted metered?
[00:07:37] Sofia: recommend dedicated slice for representing production behavior for checkout; personalization can be hosted meter with adaptive slices.
[00:07:45] Marcus: anything else re legal/procurement?
[00:07:48] Sofia: procurement will need SOW and terms; i'll loop in our contract specialist. we can also do a limited PO trial.
[00:07:55] Priya: great. can you run through an example policy JSON for rate limits?
[00:08:00] [00:08:00] Jae: reading snippet on screen — example policy: {"orgCap":5000000, "projects": [{"id":"checkout","reserve":0.4, "hardLimit":true}, {"id":"personalization","reserve":0.2, "burst": true}], "fallbackPolicy":"preempt-low-priority"}. note: pseudo-json in screen share, but actual policy can be edited in console.
[00:08:26] Marcus: i noticed the fallback policy mentions "preempt-low-priority" — does that perform model fallback or token-level shedding?
[00:08:33] Jae: it's configurable. by default we try model fallback (smaller variant), then per-request queueing with jitter, then shedding at token-level if still overloaded.
[00:08:44] Ethan: logging of fallbacks? we need to trace why a request got downgraded.
[00:08:48] Luis: we emit events with reason codes: FallbackModel, QueueExceeded, RateLimit. those appear in the trace and usage logs for auditing.
[00:08:59] Priya: anything about cold start for warmed KV cache when keys are sticky?
[00:09:03] Jae: yes, warmup windows can be set; you can pin cache warmers to some slices to reduce cold-start latency. the Console has a warmup plan UI.
[00:09:12] Marcus: we're also thinking about multi-region. can routing enforce region affinity for data residency?
[00:09:18] Jae: yep — region-aware routing policies. you can bind project keys to region preferences, and we keep data residency and inference in-region for Private deployments.
[00:09:27] Priya: after this demo i'd like the org->project mapping template.
[00:09:31] Sofia: Jae will share it.
[00:09:33] [00:09:33] Jae: sharing link in chat: https://redwood.ai/console/orgkey-template (note: link is a placeholder for shared artifact).
[00:09:41] Marcus: what about sudden DDoS or noisy tenants? can we rate-limit at IP layer or token-layer?
[00:09:47] Luis: both. we have edge rate-limiting and per-key throttles; also sticky token buckets per project key so noisy tenants can be quarantined.
[00:09:57] Ethan: fine, we'll need WAF integration details in the security pack.
[00:10:01] Sofia: we'll include WAF and SIEM integration docs.
[00:10:05] Priya: any mention of cost controls — alerts on spend?
[00:10:08] Luis: yes, org-level budget alerts, per-project spend throttles, and automatic pause when an org hits a hard spend cap.
[00:10:16] Marcus: good. show me the audit trail UI for a project key.
[00:10:20] [00:10:20] Jae: (screen) audit view shows request id, api key, route, duration, reason codes; you can filter by fallbacks. you can also export to S3 or BigQuery.
[00:10:33] Ethan: about the pilot — if we provision Dedicated slice for checkout, what SLA do we get?
[00:10:37] Sofia: Dedicated comes with SLA for uptime and latency tiers in the contract; we'll share the SLA appendix.
[00:10:44] Priya: curious about how rolling deploys affect capacity — if you push a new model, do we see an outage?
[00:10:49] Jae: rolling deploys are gradual with canary routing, and runtime has graceful connection draining; KV cache is preserved where possible. we also provide automatic fallback to previous model if regressions detected.
[00:11:03] Marcus: can Optimize surface quality regressions after model changes?
[00:11:07] Jae: yes — Optimize hooks to your eval prompts and will alert with regression score and examples.
[00:11:14] Priya: what about tokenization differences across model variants affecting costing?
[00:11:18] Luis: we show token breakdown per-model and project; Optimize will recommend model variants that minimize token churn for your prompts.
[00:11:26] Marcus: ok looks solid.
[00:11:28] [00:11:28] (fast forward dialogue snippets through middle of call as E2E demo continues, simulated load tests, more Q&A)
[00:28:05] Priya: follow-up: will you provide an example SLA appendix and pilot SOW?
[00:28:10] Sofia: yes, we'll attach SOW and a sample SLA.
[00:28:15] Marcus: timeline recap — pilot start Tues, run 2 weeks, metrics: p95 < 120ms for checkout, baseline 800 QPS burst to 1k QPS, security artifacts delivered before pilot.
[00:28:30] Ethan: i'll need contact for legal and compliance review.
[00:28:33] Sofia: i'll cc our contracts and privacy team.
[00:28:37] Jae: quick technical note: for the pilot we recommend a small Dedicated slice with a 20% overprovision to ensure KV warming; Optimize will take a 24-48 hour profiling run to tune batch sizes.
[00:28:50] Priya: agree.
[00:28:52] Marcus: any blockers from Redwood side?
[00:28:55] Sofia: just finalizing SOW and capacity allocation; otherwise we can start.
[00:29:00] [00:29:00] (end of demo, wrap up and logistics)
[00:29:05] Sofia: recap of next steps: send pilot pricing, org->project mapping template, SOC2/security pack, schedule kickoff invite.
[00:29:12] Marcus: sounds good.
[00:29:14] Priya: thanks everyone.
[00:29:16] Ethan: thank you.
[00:29:18] Sofia: i'll follow up with the items and calendar.
[00:29:22] (call ends, small bit of crosstalk)
